(B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

findings.citation_text: 3-501.18(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Disposition. (A) A FOOD specified in 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in 3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or PACKAGE that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in 3-501.17(A).

findings.comment:

410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Training programs must be accredited by the American National Standards Institute or another reputable accreditation agency under the ASTM International E2659-09 (Standard Practice for Certificate Programs). findings.comment:
Observed a member staff to not use a barrier when turning off hand sink after washing hands. Discussed with PIC, education was provided on proper hand washing. Ensure staff is properly washing. 

2-301.12: (A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of arms for at least 20 seconds. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use proper procedure (C) To prevent recontamination, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use barrier to operate faucet handles. (D) Automatic handwashing facility may be used if APPROVED.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
Inspector observed the sanitizer dispensing unit to not be dispensing sanitizer. The sanitizer bucket pulled from the unit also tested at 0 ppm Quat. Discussed with PIC, the sanitizer was not plugged into dispenser. The sanitizer would not stay plugged in so a work order has been placed, yet it was still able to provided the correct amount of concentration when manually held in place.  Service will be called for and the inspector will conduct a follow up inspection. Ensure facility has sanitizer available and at the correct concentration at all hours of operation. 

4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have minimum temperature (55F), concentration (100ppm), and pH (10). (B) Iodine shall have 68F, pH of 5 or less and concentration of 12.5ppm and 25ppm. (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have 75F, concentration based on label, and water with 500ppm hardness or less. (D) - (E) Meets EPA-label use and regulatory authority approval. (P) (F) Other chemical sanitizers in-use shall have EPA-registered label, display device registration number on device and is operated and maintained in accordance with manufacturers instructions (Pf)

findings.title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties
findings.comment:
Inspector observed priority and priority foundation items during the inspection today. Ensure that person in charge is actively aware of what constitutes Priority and Priority foundation items and takes measures to avoid these violations whenever possible. PIC was coached on temperature logs for the cold holding units, using test strips daily for the chemical sanitizer dispenser in the facility. The violation is considered corrected on site.  

2-102.11: Based on the RISKS inherent to the FOOD operation, PIC shall demonstrate knowledge by:  (A) Having no Priority Foundation items; (B) Being a CFM; OR (C) Responding correctly questions as they relate to the specific FOOD operation. The areas of knowledge include C1 through C16.

findings.title: No bare hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed
findings.comment:
Inspector observed an employee place their bare hand on lettuce in an attempt to determine the lettuce temperature. Bare hand contact with ready to eat food is not allowed. Refrain from touching foods that no longer need to be washed or cooked with bare hands. The employee was coached immediately and the lettuce was then discarded in the garbage. The violation is considered corrected on site.  

3-301.11: (A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall properly wash hands (C). (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall not contact RTE FOODS with bare hands  except washing fruits and veggies (P). (C) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall minimize contact with FOOD that is not RTE (Pf). (D) Contact does not apply to RTE Food being added as ingredient to be cooked. (E) FOOD EMPLOYEES not serving a HSP may contact exposed, RTE with bare hands if approved.

4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment:
Inspector observed three cold holding units where food was being held out of temperature:
1) The cooler across from the grill area has a bottom left drawer holding 3 bs of ribs at 45.5F and 3 lbs of Philly meat at 47.2F. These meats were discarded in the garbage. Other items in the cooler top left drawer (ham 39), right side upper and lower drawers are holding various cheeses between 38F and 40F. Service will be called to ensure that the unit is functioning properly. Use unit properly as well. Do not put hot foods in the unit to cool (plastic wrap on ribs had condensation drops on it) and keep unit pulled out away from the wall so that air flow is not restricted.  Thermometer in the unit read 38F
2) The cooler on the left at salad (with drawers) is holding cut fruit with melon at 47F, a single bottle of house made salad dressing at 46F, and lettuce at 47F and 49F. These items were discarded in the garbage. Use cooler properly by keeping the top filled with pans or lids at all times. Lettuce in the left side top drawer of this unit was in a tightly closed bag in a pan. The lettuce on the right was in a pan that is too big to properly fit in the unit. The cut fruit was in a mixing bowl that was in a pan. Do not double pan food items that are placed in prep cooler for cold holding. Thermometer in the unit reads 42F. The unit will be evaluated. Other items in the top of the unit are between 38 and 41F. Keep an eye on this unit today. The internal thermometer has raised from 42F to 45F.  Temperature of food in the top of the make table has raised to 44F. The unit is no longer going to be used. Items from the top of the unit were moved to the walk in. 
3) The make table in the snack bar has 4 cups of pre packaged guacamole labeled keep refrigerated at 45F. The independent thermometer in the unit reads 41F. The cups of guacamole were discarded. The snack bar will not open until labor day. All snack bar equipment will be cleaned and evaluated before being put into use. 
Food temperature violations are considered corrected on site. Ensure that units are working and being used properly for food safety. 
3-501.16: (A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. (B) EGGS not treated to destroy Salmonellae shall be stored at 45F or less.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
Inspector observed a house made dressing in a squeeze bottle in the top of the salad make table on the left. The contents of the bottle were 46F. The dressing was not labeled with a date marking. The bottle was in a pan in the top of the unit. The contents of the bottle were discarded. Take care not to double pan items in make tables. Mark all TCS ready to eat foods with 7 day date markings. The violation is considered corrected on site. 

3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf). (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date (Pf). (C) Combined portions of food shall retain the date marking of the earliest-prepared food (Pf). (D) Approved date marking systems (C). (E)  Does not apply to repacked from a bulk container (C). (F) Does not apply to shellstock (C).  (G) Exemptions: prepared deli salads prepared according to 21 CFR 110; hard cheeses (39% moisture); semi-soft cheeses (50% or less); cultured dairy products (yogurt, sour cream, buttermilk); preserved fish (pickled herring, dried/salted); dry, fermented sausages (pepperoni); and salt-cured products (prosciutto and parma).

findings.title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
findings.comment:
Inspector observed whisks in the kitchen stored in a container with their handles down and food contact surfaces up so that they had to be touched in order to remove the whisks from the container. Store food equipment properly protected. 

4-903.11: (A) clean FOOD-CONTACT surfaces shall be stored: in clean, dry location, not exposed to splash or other contamination, and at least 6 inches above floor. (B) clean EQUIPMENT shall be stored in self-draining position that allows air drying, covered or inverted. (D) Items that are kept in closed PACKAGES may be stored below 6 inches if on dollies, pallets, racks, and skids properly designed.

findings.title: Single-use/single-service articles: properly stored and used
findings.comment:
Inspector observed boxes of single use cups on the floor in the dry storage area of the basement. There is also a stack of paper boats in the dry storage stored with food contact surfaces up and exposed to dust and soil. Store all clean articles properly protected. 

4-903.11: (A) clean EQUIPMENT and clean ARTICLES shall be stored in clean, dry location where they are not exposed to contamination and at least 6 inches above the floor. (C) SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be kept in original PACKAGE or stored in manner to protect it against contamination.

findings.comment:
Inspector observed a baking mat with slices through it and a spatula with cracks and a gouge. These items were discarded as they are not longer smooth or easily cleanable. Take note of equipment condition and discard when it is no longer in compliance with this section.

P Materials used for FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES may not allow migration of deleterious substances shall be: (B) Durable, nonabsorbent, and CORROSION-RESISTANT (C) Sufficient in weight and thickness (D) SMOOTH, EASILY CLEANABLE surface (E) Resistant to pitting, chipping, scratching, decomposition, and distortion. findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
Inspector observed the snack bar kitchen to have accumulated and encrusted soil in the oven, low boy drawers, under the grills on the low boy, in the prep top lid of the make table. The facility was closed in the fall and the facility has not been used since that time according to the staff. 

4-601.11: (B) The FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking EQUIPMENT and pans shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other soil accumulations. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
The facility has a vent to the right of the opening to the chef’s office. The vent has an accumulation of dust. The vent is a draw and therefore collects dust and dirt. The exit light also has an accumulation of dust on it. Clean this area and maintain it clean. 

6-501.12: (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

Observed the following food-contact areas to be soiled with dust/debris/food splash:
1. The shelving unit across from the 3 compartment sink in the upstairs kitchen has dust on it - clean salad bowls and other cooking utensils are being placed on top. The ceiling above this prep area also has a layer of dust. Clean plates are above the area.
2. There is a vent next to the kitchen manager’s office where a shelving unit has clean dish ware. The vent is severely soiled with a layer of dust and the shelving unit with these clean utensils is also dusty.
3. The dessert prep area (across from the cook line in this area) has a layer of dust on the ceiling above the food-contact surfaces.
4. One prep cooler and the reach-in freezer within the basement kitchen had significant food splash (salad, shred cheese - prep cooler; spilled frozen chicken, tater tots, fries - reach-in freezer). Ensure staff is aware to clean the interior of the cold holding units to keep food splash minimal. 
5. The interior of the microwave in the downstairs kitchen has food splash within it.

Ensure maintenance and kitchen staff are aware to keep clean food-contact surfaces (or areas above food-contact surfaces) free of dust and debris - wash, rinse, sanitize. Discussed with kitchen manager and facility manager. Inspector will follow-up to ensure the areas are clean by 9/11/23.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.112: (A) Temperature of the fresh hot water SANITIZING rinse may not be more than 194F or less than 165F for stationary rack, single temperature machines. All other machines can be no less than 180F. (B) Maximum temperature does not apply to high pressure and temperature systems with wand-type spraying devices. 

Observed the downstairs kitchen dish machine to be ~128F after multiple runs were conducted. The temperature of the machine should be 160F to 194F. Facility has a maximum registering thermometer to check heated dish machine temperatures. Ensure staff routinely uses the thermometer to verify the heated dish machine temperatures both upstairs and downstairs at the two dish machines. Repair service (GFS) was called during the inspection to correct the dish machine. The downstairs kitchen is currently in use due to still having the pool area open for the year. Ensure the staff is aware NOT to use this dish machine as it is not heat sanitizing properly. Ensure the staff only utilizes the 3 compartment sink to wash, rinse, and sanitize until the dish machine is repaired. Discussed with the kitchen and facility managers. Inspector will follow-up on 9/11/23.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment:
3-501.16: (A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. (B) EGGS not treated to destroy Salmonellae shall be stored at 45F or less. 

Observed the second salad prep cooler (with the dressings at the top prep cooler) to be out of temperature. Ambient air in the cooler was ~55F in the back and ~62F in the front of the bottom of the prep cooler. Probed items included: raw chicken (69F), pork belly (51F), cottage cheese (52F). Items were voluntarily discarded along with dairy-based dressings, sour cream tubs (2x), mayonnaise tub, and sardine tins (2x). Discussed with kitchen and facility managers. Cease use of the cooler until AirMaster’s arrives to fix the cooler. Inspector will follow-up on 9/6/23 (holiday weekend - facility and SCDPH are closed).

findings.title: Approved thawing methods used
findings.comment:
3-501.13: TCS FOOD shall be thawed: (A) at 41F or below in refrigeration (B) completely submerged under running water, not getting above 41F (water temp of 70F or below). If food will be cooked, not getting above 41F for more than 4 hours. (C) part of the cooking process (D) Using any procedure if RTE FOOD is thawed and prepared for immediate service (E) ROP FISH that bear label shall be removed from packaging before thawing under refrigeration, upon completion of thawing from running water. 

Observed the thawed salmon in the cold holding drawer along the upstairs cook line to be within the packaging still. The packages states on each salmon to remove the packaging prior to thawing. Discussed with kitchen manager and cook at the line. Change practices on how facility is thawing salmon. Remove from packaging prior to thawing. COS.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
findings.comment:
4-904.11: (A) cleaned and SANITIZED UTENSILS shall be handled, displayed, and dispensed to prevent FOOD- and lip-contact surface contamination. (B) UTENSILS not prewrapped shall be presented so only handles are touched by EMPLOYEES and/or CONSUMERS. (C) SINGLE-SERVCIE ARTICLES intended for FOOD- and lip-contact shall be furnished for CONSUMER with wrapper or APPROVED dispenser. 

Observed multiple areas within the upstairs kitchen with plates and bowls turned right side up so food- and lip-contact surfaces were exposed (along all the prep lines on the top shelves and in the dessert area prep across from the vacuum sealer machine). Cease practice. Ensure all plates, bowls, dish ware, and cookware are flipped over to prevent cross contamination. Discussed with kitchen manager. Correct by next routine inspection.

Ensure repairs and/or replacements are available for the next routine inspection. Discussed with kitchen and facility managers. This is a repeat violation since the last routine inspection on 4/21/23.

Discussed routine cleaning with PIC’s. Ensure the above areas are cleaned before the next routine inspection.

findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625 and IAC Section 750.3430 (C) Facility is not in compliance with the food handler law. All food handlers, other than someone who has the food service sanitation manager certificate, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code. Food handlers working at a temporary food establishment are exempt from this requirement.  

Observed the majority of the food handler’s cards for the front of the house to be expired (seasonal workers mainly). Discussed with facility manager. Facility manager ordered 35 food handler tests to be taken by the staff over a period of time soon. Facility will ensure the staff re-takes food handler’s training and keep updated copies in the public health folder. Correct by next routine inspection.

findings.title: Allergen training as required
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625/3.07 Sec. 3.07. Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter.

(REPEAT) Observed no allergen training certification for all the certified food protection manager’s (CFPM’s). Discussed with PIC’s. Ensure all CFPM’s take the allergen training certification and print copies for the facility public health license folder. Correct by next routine inspection. Provided educational hand out on where to take this course online. This is a repeat violation since the last routine inspection on 4/21/23.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.comment:
4-501.11: (A) EQUIPMENT shall be maintained in good repair. (B) EQUIPMENT components shall be kept intact, tight, and adjusted to manufacturer’s specifications. (C) Cutting or piercing parts of can opens shall be kept sharp to minimize metal fragmentation. 

Observed the walk-in freezer in the upstairs kitchen to have ponding water at the base on the floor. Discussed with Chef. Chef stated he would contact Air Master’s to have them look at the walk-in freezer. Water should not be ponding at the base flooring of the walk-in. Correct before next routine inspection.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
4-601.11: (B) The FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking EQUIPMENT and pans shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other soil accumulations. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

Observed the following areas in need of cleaning (non-food contact surfaces):
1. Walk-in freezer floor (upstairs kitchen) needs swept of debris.
2. Ceilings in the dessert prep area need cleaned of dust (ceiling tiles and vents - minor dust).
3. Dry storage downstairs has a spill on the floor under shelving - clean.

Discussed routine cleaning of the above areas with PIC. Correct before next routine inspection.

findings.title: Allergen training as required
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625/3.07 Sec. 3.07. Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter.

Observed no allergen training certifications for the CFPM’s. Discussed with Chef and main manager of facility. Provided educational handout on how to take the allergen training certification course. Ensure all certified food protection manager’s complete allergen training certification and copies of the license are printed for the facility. Correct by next routine inspection.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment:
4-501.19: The temperature of the wash solution in manual WAREWASHING EQUIPMENT shall be maintained at not less than 110F or the temperature specified on the cleaning agent manufacturer's label instructions.

Observed no heat test strips or a maximum registering thermometer. Discussed with PIC. PIC is ordering a max registering thermometer for the dish machine. Inspector will follow-up on 1/16/23.

findings.title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties
findings.comment:
2-102.11: Based on the RISKS inherent to the FOOD operation, PIC shall demonstrate knowledge by:  (A) Having no Priority Foundation items; (B) Being a CFM; OR (C) Responding correctly questions as they relate to the specific FOOD operation. The areas of knowledge include C1 through C16.  

The dispenser for quat based sanitizer in the kitchen is observed to not be functioning correctly at the time of the inspection. Per the PIC, MJ Kelner has been contacted to service the machine but has not yet conducted it. Follow up set for the beginning of the year due to holidays. Sanitizers at the facility are observed correct at this time as employees are making the solution manually.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment:
4-302.14: A test kit or other device that accurately measures the concentration in MG/L of SANITIZING solutions shall be provided. 

The facility uses temperature sanitizing dish machines, but does not have a method to verify that the dishes in these unit are reaching critical temperature. PIC indicated that a “disk” type thermometer would be ordered on the large order at the beginning of the year. Follow up set for the first Friday of January.

findings.title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties
findings.comment:
2-102.11: Based on the RISKS inherent to the FOOD operation, PIC shall demonstrate knowledge by:  (A) Having no Priority Foundation items; (B) Being a CFM; OR (C) Responding correctly questions as they relate to the specific FOOD operation. The areas of knowledge include C1 through C16.  

The dispenser for quat based sanitizer in the kitchen is observed to not be functioning correctly at the time of the inspection. Per the PIC, MJ Kelner services this machine and has been contacted during this inspection. Inspector will follow up in two weeks to ensure repair is completed.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.comment:
2-102.12: (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM. 

A the time of this inspection a CFPM certificate was not available for anyone at the facility. The current kitchen manager is in the process of  completing this requirement and also stated that each kitchen employee was on a list for sequential certification. They were given a sheet with the current CFPM courses as well as the SCDPH courses for next year.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
2-301.14: FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including (A)-(I) any activities that may have contaminated the hands.  

Multiple employees are observed to don gloves without hand washing prior. PIC was consulted and education took place. Hand washing should always take place directly prior to donning gloves. PIC should ensure employee training and enforce compliance with the code.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
5-202.12: (A) HANDWASHING SINK shall be equipped to provide water of a temperature at least 100F through mixing valve. Pf (B) Steam mixing valve may not be used. (C) A self-closing, slow-closing, or metered faucet shall provide at least 15 seconds of flowing water. (D) An automatic sink shall be installed to manufacturer’s guidelines. 

The only hand sink in the main cooking area is observed without hot water available. PIC was consulted. The plumber on staff should be available to conduct repairs starting tomorrow. Inspector will follow up in two weeks for compliance.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
(REPEAT x2) 4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

The potato slicer is observed with dried on food debris. PIC was consulted and the item was moved to cleaning during the inspection to correct.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria. 

The sani buckets in the facility are observed to register either no sanitizer or low sanitizer on the inspector’s test strips. Investigation revealed that the dispenser is not properly providing sanitizer at the initial dispensation point. The buckets were remade during this inspection to correct the immediate violation. Refer to line item #1 for dispenser follow up.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf). (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date (Pf). (C) Combined portions of food shall retain the date marking of the earliest-prepared food (Pf). (D) Approved date marking systems (C).

A gallon of milk is observed in the underside of the prep cooler across from the fryers without a date mark. The container has been mostly used and the current day worker is unaware of when it was opened, indicating at least prior day service. The same container has a use by date of 11/30/22 (two days ago). A discussion took place with the PIC and the item discarded during this inspection to correct.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment:
4-302.14: A test kit or other device that accurately measures the concentration in MG/L of SANITIZING solutions shall be provided. 

1) The facility uses temperature sanitizing dish machines, but do not have a method to verify that the dishes in these unit are reaching critical temperature. Inspector discussed with the PIC and showed examples of both single use strips and maximum registering thermometers that would be sufficient.  2) The facility uses a quat based sanitizer in the sani buckets as well as the three part sinks (upstairs in the main kitchen as well as the downstairs outside bar area) but does not currently have any test strips for this chemical.  PIC is aware that a verification method is required for all sanitizers used in the facility. Inspector will follow-up in two weeks for compliance.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
4-602.13: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues. 

Multiple shelves in the upstairs walk in cooler are observed with thick accumulations of mold/food debris, specifically the shelves to the right as you enter said cooler. PIC instructed to ensure that the shelves are cleaned at a frequency to preclude the accumulation of soilage.

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used
findings.comment:
6-403.11: (B) Lockers or other suitable facilities shall be located in a designated room or area where contamination of FOOD, EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES cannot occur. 

1) A bottle of Body Armor drink is observed in the cooler across from the fryers mixed in with foods intended for consumers. 2) A bottle of “Liquid Death” thirst quencher is observed in the reach in cooler under the soup hot holding station mixed in with foods intended for consumers. PIC was consulted about both locations and storage of employee beverages/foods in general. Items should be segregated from those intended for consumers with a preference of below and away from items intended for consumers. Drinks were moved during the inspection to correct the violation.

findings.title: No bare hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed
findings.comment:
3-801.11: (D) FOOD EMPLOYEES may not contact READY-TO-EAT FOOD as specified under  3-301.11(B) and (E). 

The ice scoop in the server area is observed with the handle in contact with the ice. This presents a concern when the hands of the server retrieve the scoop and make contact with the Ready-To-Eat foods (ice). Scoop was removed during the inspection to correct.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

1) the meat slicer in the front prep area is observed soiled with food debris; 2) a large cast iron skillet next to the meat slicer is observed soiled with food debris; 3) (REPEAT) The potato slicer is observed with dried on food debris. PIC was consulted and all items were moved to cleaning during the inspection to correct.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
findings.comment:
4-903.11: (A) clean FOOD-CONTACT surfaces shall be stored: in clean, dry location, not exposed to splash or other contamination, and at least 6 inches above floor. (B) clean EQUIPMENT shall be stored in self-draining position that allows air drying, covered or inverted. (D) Items that are kept in closed PACKAGES may be stored below 6 inches if on dollies, pallets, racks, and skids properly designed. 

1) Utensils used for making drinks in the upstairs bar area are in containers with soiled bottoms. Containers and utensils were moved to dish for cleaning during the inspection to correct. 2) The scoop holder for the ice scoop in the server area is observed with black mold developing in the bottom. The holder was moved to dish during the inspection to correct. 3) Cleaned/sanitized ladles are stored hanging from a shelf behind a hot box in the main kitchen. The utensils in question are in contact with and right behind the exhaust vent for this unit. This posses a potential contamination concern. The scoops were moved to dish and the location will not be used in the future.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment:
4-302.14: A test kit or other device that accurately measures the concentration in MG/L of SANITIZING solutions shall be provided. 

1) The facility uses temperature sanitizing dish machines, but do not have a method to verify that the dishes in these unit are reaching critical temperature. Inspector discussed with the PIC and showed examples of both single use strips and maximum registering thermometers that would be sufficient. A small amount of single use strips were acquired during the inspection to correct the violation. 2) The facility uses a quat based sanitizer in the sani buckets as well as the three part sinks (upstairs in the main kitchen as well as the downstairs outside bar area) but does not currently have any test strips for this chemical. A small amount were acquired during the inspection to correct. PIC is aware that a verification method is required for all sanitizers used int he facility.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
4-602.13: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues. 

1) Multiple shelves throughout the kitchen are observed with minor soilage and are in need of cleaning. 2) the lip behind the prep line coolers in the main kitchen is in need of cleaning. 3) The shelves in the front part of the kitchen are in need of cleaning. 4) The frame of the standing cooler next to the PICs office is in need of cleaning. 5) The handle of the microwave is in need of cleaning. PIC instructed to ensure that all nonfood contact locations are maintained clean.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.12: (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing. 

1) The floor in multiple locations throughout the facility are in need of cleaning, specifically under equipment and shelving. 2) The ceiling vent over the prep line coolers is heavily soiled with dust. 3) Soda syrup was spilled and not completely cleaned in the dry storage area. PIC instructed to clean often enough so as to maintain the facility clean.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.comment:
2-102.12: (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM. 

At the time of the inspection, no CFPM is available at the facility. The PIC (Ben) stated that they would be taking the course/ test in the near future. A CFPM should be available at the facility at all times that food and/or food contact are being handled. A hand out was given with the current CFPM courses known by SCDPH in this area.

findings.title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated
findings.comment:
3-202.15: FOOD packages shall be in good condition and protect the integrity of the contents so that the FOOD is not exposed to ADULTERATION or potential contaminants. 

Four cans on the rack in the dry storage area are observed with significant dents along the seam welds. Cans were separated for discard/ credit during the inspection to correct. PIC is instructed to review with employees about what items should be set aside as Opposed to storing for use.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

The potato slicer is observed with dried on food debris. PIC was consulted and the item moved to dish for cleaning.

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored
findings.comment:
3-304.12: FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored: (A) in FOOD with their handles above top of FOOD and container (B) In non-TCS FOOD (C) On clean portion of FOOD preparation table or cooking EQUIPMENT as long as UTENSIL cleaned with proper frequency (Time/Temp Control Form). (D) In running water with sufficient velocity (E) In clean, protected location if UTENSILS are used only for FOOD not TCS (F) In container of water at least 135F and container is properly cleaned. 

An in-use knife is observed stored in the gap between the prep coolers across from the grills. PIC was consulted and the knife moved to dish to correct. PIC instructed to review with staff in relation to utensil storage.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
findings.comment:
4-903.11: (A) clean FOOD-CONTACT surfaces shall be stored: in clean, dry location, not exposed to splash or other contamination, and at least 6 inches above floor. (B) clean EQUIPMENT shall be stored in self-draining position that allows air drying, covered or inverted. (D) Items that are kept in closed PACKAGES may be stored below 6 inches if on dollies, pallets, racks, and skids properly designed. 

Two quarter pans are observed sitting on their sides in the water of an inactive steam well. PIC was consulted and the pans moved to dish to correct. Cleaned items should be protected from any potential source of contamination prior to use.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment:
4-303.11: (A) Cleaning agents used to clean EQUIPMENT shall be provided and available during all hours of operation. (B) Chemical SANITIZERS shall be provided and available during all hours of operation. 

On arrival, no sani buckets were available in any of the food preparation or handling areas. The full kitchen is in the process of prepping for an event taking place this afternoon as well as normal service operations. PIC stated that buckets had not yet been made at this time. Inspector stated that sanitizers should be available for use at all times that food preparation and/or handling is taking place. Buckets were made during the inspection to correct.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf). (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date (Pf). (C) Combined portions of food shall retain the date marking of the earliest-prepared food (Pf). (D) Approved date marking systems (C). 

1) Milk in the snack bar cooler directly behind the cashier is observed without a date mark. 2) Milk in the reach in cooler in the server area directly off the kitchen is observed without a date mark. Inspector discussed with the PIC and the items were labeled during the inspection to correct or discarded.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
4-601.11: (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

1) Multiple sets of shelves in multiple coolers are observed with an accumulation of food debris. 2) Lids on multiple containers in the walk in cooler upstairs are observed soiled. 3) A microwave in the main kitchen and another in the snack bar kitchen are observed soiled. Multiple shelves used for storming food containers or cooking equipment are observed with food debris and dust. PIC instructed to clean non food contact surfaces often enough to prevent the accumulation of debris/residue.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
2-301.12: (A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of arms for at least 20 seconds. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use proper procedure (C) To prevent recontamination, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use barrier to operate faucet handles. (D) Automatic handwashing facility may be used if APPROVED. 

An employee in the main kitchen was observed to wash their hands, then turn off the faucet with their bare hands and then reach for a paper towel to dry. Insepctor discussed proper hand washing procedure with the PIC and instructed them to review with employees.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
6-301.12: Each HANDWASHING SINK shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; (C) A heated-air hand drying device; (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures. 

The hand sink in the bar area is observed without and approved hand drying system. The employee on duty stated that dish towels are used to dry hands after washing. Inspector discussed with the PIC and instructed them to have an approved method in place for drying hands after hand washing. Fruits appear to be sliced for drinks at this station. Paper towels were made available during the inspection to correct.

findings.title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated
findings.comment:
3-202.15: FOOD packages shall be in good condition and protect the integrity of the contents so that the FOOD is not exposed to ADULTERATION or potential contaminants. 

Multiple cans of foods (brown beans, tomatoes, tomato puree, black beans) in the dry storage area are observed with large dents. Inspector discussed with the PIC and the cans were moved to discard during the inspection to correct.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment:
3-501.16: (A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. (B) EGGS not treated to destroy Salmonellae shall be stored at 45F or less. 

The prep cooler across from the grill in the snack bar is observed holding foods with internal temperatures between 48 and 53 degrees. Foods include sliced tomatoes and chicken salad. The space in the bottom of this cooler is also out of temperature and includes hot dogs, chicken, hamburgers and steaks also observed with internal temperatures between 48 and 53 degrees. Foods were discarded during the inspection and a call placed to air masters during the inspection to correct. Inspector will spot check to ensure maintenance is completed on the cooler.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition

3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf). (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date (Pf). (C) Combined portions of food shall retain the date marking of the earliest-prepared food (Pf). (D) Approved date marking systems (C). 

1) Milk in the snack bar cooler directly behind the cashier is observed without a date mark. 2) Cooked/ cooled pulled pork and taco meat in the snack bar walk in cooler are observed without a date mark. 3) Milk in the reach in cooler in the server area directly off the kitchen is observed without a date mark. Inspector discussed with the PIC and the items were labeled during the inspection to correct.

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored
findings.comment:
3-304.12: FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored: (A) in FOOD with their handles above top of FOOD and container (B) In non-TCS FOOD (C) On clean portion of FOOD preparation table or cooking EQUIPMENT as long as UTENSIL cleaned with proper frequency (Time/Temp Control Form). (D) In running water with sufficient velocity (E) In clean, protected location if UTENSILS are used only for FOOD not TCS (F) In container of water at least 135F and container is properly cleaned. 

In use knives are observed stored in the crack between prep tables: 1) in the snack bar across from the grill and, 2) in the main kitchen between the salad prep coolers. Locations are not easily cleaned. Knives were moved to the respective dish areas and will be stored in an approved fashion moving forward.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) and (B)  (P) TCS foods in the bottom section of the right hand prep cooler next to the grill in the kitchen are observed with internal temperatures between 45 and 47 degrees. Sliced meats, rice and sliced cheese were discarded to correct. Inspector will spot check in the future to ensure proper effectiveness of the cooler.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114  (P) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution. Options: 25ppm to 49ppm when the temperature is at least 120°F and the pH is 10 or less; or (2) 50ppm to 99ppm when the temperature is at least 100°F and the pH is 10 or less, or when the temperature is at least 75°F and the pH is 8 or less; or (3) 100ppm when the temperature is at least 55°F and the pH is 10 or less. The dish machine in the bar area registered 0 ppm CL on the inspector's and facility's test strips. Eichanauer was contacted during the inspection for maintenance. The facility will take items in need of cleaning to the dish machine in the kitchen until maintenance can be completed.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.citation_text: 4-602.13  (C) Clean all non-food contact surfaces frequently to prevent soil accumulation.  The shelves in the walk in cooler are observed soiled. PIC is instructed to clean the shelves often enough to keep them clean. It is suggested to begin a cleaning cycle to clean sections of shelves regularly as time permits.

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used
findings.citation_text: 6-305.11  (C) Food establishments shall A) Provide designated dressing rooms or dressing areas for employees that routinely change their clothes in the establishment; B) Provide lockers or other suitable facilities for the orderly storage of employees' clothing and other possessions. Two cell phones were observed on a wire shelf over cleaned/ sanitized dishes and utensils. Employee belongings should be stored so that they are not over cleaned and sanitized food contact surfaces. The phones were removed during the inspection to correct.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display

findings.title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
findings.citation_text:
4-903.11 (A) (1) (C) Cleaned EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, laundered LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE USE ARTICLES shall be stored in a clean, dry location.
